course.title: AP World History: Modern
course.description: Understand the people, ideas, and connections that shaped the world from c. 1200 to the present.
course.previewDescription: Explore how states rose, belief systems spread, trade networks connected regions, and revolutions reshaped societies from c. 1200 to the present.

themes.title: Interactions of humans with the environment
themes.question: How did geography, crops, resources, or disease shape choices?
themes.example: Andean terraces made steep slopes more usable for farming.

themes.title: Social interactions and organization
themes.question: Who had status, opportunities, or obligations?
themes.example: Examination preparation favored families that could afford education.

themes.title: Political systems and governance
themes.question: How did rulers gain authority and administer territory?
themes.example: Song officials carried imperial decisions into local government.

themes.title: Economic systems
themes.question: How were goods produced, exchanged, taxed, or distributed?
themes.example: Mali drew revenue from commerce through its territory.

themes.title: Cultural developments and interactions
themes.question: How did beliefs, learning, and artistic practices influence society?
themes.example: Buddhist monasteries connected religious practice with education.

themes.title: Technology and innovation
themes.question: What techniques or tools changed what people could do?
themes.example: Inca roads and knotted records helped officials coordinate resources.

lesson.title: Continuity and Change in a Globalized World
lesson.summary: What changed, and what stayed the same, as the world became more connected.
learningGoals: Explain the extent to which globalization changed the world from 1900 to the present.
lesson.bigIdea: Globalization greatly increased the speed and scale of exchange, but older patterns of inequality and state power persisted.
lesson.context: Continuity and change over time is an AP reasoning process. Strong answers describe both what changed and what stayed the same.

sections.title: Faster, larger, and still unequal

blocks.text: Globalization, the growing connection of the world's economies, cultures, and peoples, is not new; trade networks linked distant regions for centuries. After 1900, technology made exchange much faster and larger in scale.
Some patterns continued. Many former colonies still export raw materials, wealth remains unequal between and within countries, and states still defend their borders and interests.

blocks.title: Cause and effect
blocks.text: Technology and new institutions accelerated exchange, while older economic structures and state interests limited how much changed.

sections.takeaway: Globalization changed the speed and scale of exchange more than its basic patterns.

vocabulary.definition: The growing connection of the world's economies, cultures, and peoples through trade, technology, and migration.

connections.title: Old networks, new speed
connections.body: Networks of exchange in the Silk Roads and Indian Ocean linked regions long before modern globalization.
connections.transferQuestion: What is new about globalization after 1900?
connections.feedback: Compare the speed or scale of exchange with an earlier network.

glossary.definition: The growing connection of the world's economies, cultures, and peoples through trade, technology, and migration.
